headline: GCC asked Russia at Manama Sunday to use UN influence to press Iran to halt attacks on Gulf states
dek: Lavrov visits Tehran Monday for bilateral + regional consultations (third Putin-Pezeshkian meeting in a month happened last week in Awaza, Turkmenistan). At Sunday's Manama meeting with GCC foreign ministers, the bloc called on Russia to use its UN influence to press Iran to halt attacks on…
sources: Iranian Foreign Ministry (visit announcement, via IRNA/ISNA/Reuters); The National (Manama meeting + plan); Iranian envoy Kazem Jalali (X, Sunday)
fault_line: Is Russia an honest broker that can restrain Iran for the Gulf — or is it Iran's wartime partner and the GCC is wasting its breath? (RFI Persian framing: mediation to end the war.)

sections.what_happened: Lavrov visits Tehran Monday for bilateral + regional consultations (third Putin-Pezeshkian meeting in a month happened last week in Awaza, Turkmenistan). At Sunday's Manama meeting with GCC foreign ministers, the bloc called on Russia to use its UN influence to press Iran to halt attacks on regional neighbors and pursue serious dialogue. Lavrov presented an updated Russian plan for collective security in the Gulf: direct dialogue among coastal states plus Iraq and Jordan; quoted: 'We all believe that it is important for all the Gulf states to have their own word in how to resolve this strategic crisis.' Social posts (RFI Persian, Dunya News Urdu, IRIB Persian, Al Mayadeen, Euronews graphics) confirm visit underway today.
sections.what_verified: IRNA, ISNA, Reuters, Al Arabiya, Times of Israel all confirm the visit announcement; The National is sole source for Manama-ask + plan details (single credible backend — treat the Manama framing as one-source).
sections.what_disputed: None; Russia-Iran closeness narrative unchanged — no actual fracture, but Gulf states lobbying Moscow is real diplomacy.
sections.why_matters: The Gulf's asking Russia to leash Iran — Moscow walks into Tehran with that in its pocket. The 'split, not the bloc' demand angle.
sections.context: Background: Russia/Iran/Gulf — Lavrov in Tehran today; GCC asked Russia at Manama Sunday to use UN influence to press Iran to halt attacks on Gulf states; Lavrov tabled updated Russian collective-security plan

totw_analysis: Our read: The Gulf's asking Russia to leash Iran — Moscow walks into Tehran with that in its pocket. The 'split, not the bloc' demand angle. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Russia an honest broker that can restrain Iran for the Gulf — or is it Iran's wartime partner and the GCC is wasting its breath? (RFI Persian framing: mediation to end the war.)
